newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says will not open telecoms market alone.
newsitem.headline: Japan says will not open telecoms market alone.

text.p: Japan"s Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has told U.S. President Bill Clinton that Tokyo would consider easing regulations in the telecommunications market only if the United States and other leading economies did the same, Japan"s top government spokesman said on Friday.

In a letter to Clinton, the Japanese prime minister said Tokyo was ready to revise its offer and open the market to foreign ownership if the United States and other nations deregulated their markets, Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajimaya said.
Clinton had earlier sent a letter to Hashimoto urging Japan to scrap its regulations on foreign ownership.

Japan, the United States and 55 other countries in telecom talks at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Geneva have until Saturday to reach agreement on liberalising the global telecommunications market.
Participants are sceptical that an accord can be reached by then.
The talks are the second effort in the last year to shape a WTO pact among some 60 countries accounting for over 91 percent of global telecommunications revenues totalling over $600 billion.
"Japan will step up its efforts only in an environment in which all participants cooperate with each other," an official of the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry said.

Mitsuo Igarashi, vice minister for posts and telecommunications, made it clear in a recent news conference that there was no possibility that Japan would totally do away with foreign ownership restrictions on NTT and KDD.
